title: Accounts Administration Assistant
description:
12-Month Fixed-Term Contract

A fantastic opportunity has arisen to join the finance shared services team of a highly successful global organisation operating within a fast-paced, technology-led environment.

This 12-month fixed-term position has been created to support the continued growth of the European Shared Service Centre and offers the chance to become part of a collaborative finance team supporting multiple international business entities.

The Role

As a Travel & Expense (T&E) Administrator, you will be responsible for ensuring the accurate and timely audit of employee travel and expense claims, providing support with payment activities, and delivering excellent customer service to stakeholders across the business.

Working within a dedicated team, you will help maintain compliance with company policies, resolve employee queries and contribute to the smooth operation of the wider finance function.

Key Responsibilities
- Auditing travel and expense submissions in line with company policies and internal controls
- Reviewing and resolving employee and stakeholder queries relating to expenses and financial transactions
- Supporting regular payment runs across multiple entities
- Assisting with month-end and year-end finance processes
- Supporting the preparation of financial reports and documentation
- Investigating and resolving discrepancies in a timely manner
- Maintaining employee data in accordance with data protection requirements
- Working closely with colleagues and other departments to support efficient financial operations
- Contributing to process improvements, training and knowledge-sharing activities
- Supporting wider shared service centre activities as required
- Occasional travel to support finance projects and system implementations

Skills & Experience

The successful candidate will ideally possess:
- Previous experience within a transactional finance environment
- Experience using a Travel & Expense platform such as Concur, Chrome River or SAP
- ERP system experience, with SAP highly desirable
- Strong Microsoft Excel and Office skills
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Strong organisational and time management skills
- Effective communication and stakeholder management abilities
- A proactive approach with strong problem-solving skills
- The ability to work independently and collaboratively
- A positive, customer-focused mindset

Qualifications
- Prior experience in finance administration, accounts payable or transactional finance preferred
- AAT studies or qualification would be advantageous but are not essential

What's on Offer
- Competitive salary and benefits package
- Annual bonus opportunity
- Flexible and hybrid working arrangements
- Exposure to a global finance function within a growing international organisation
- Supportive and collaborative working environment
- Opportunity to contribute to ongoing finance transformation projects

Location

This is a hybrid position based in South Wales. Following an initial training period of approximately 12 weeks, the role will operate on a 3 days office / 2 days home working basis.

title: Contract Support Associate
description:
Company Profile

CBRE is the global leader in commercial real estate services and investment. We help our clients and communities realise their potential through industry-leading expertise, innovation, and integrated solutions.

Job Title: Contract Support Associate

As a CBRE Contract Support Associate, you will provide exceptional customer service and administrative support to a large Business Unit, Facility, or Account.

Role Summary:
- This role is part of the Contract Quality Management job function and is responsible for supporting the delivery of contractual services to ensure requirements are fulfilled.
- Respond to client inquiries and concerns and ensure timely and quality service delivery and follow-up to ensure satisfaction.
- Understand the scope of the contract and make sure that all work is carried out accordingly.
- Be a financial and operational systems champion. Suggest efforts to put in place cost-saving opportunities to maximise customer and financial savings targets.
- Coordinate and onboard vendors for reactive and planned works and manage subcontractor paperwork.
- Review processed invoices and ensure accurate cost centre coding. Coordinate the billing application, calculate margins, raise invoices, and submit to clients. Work closely with site teams and head office, ensuring accurate processing of quotations and purchase orders.
- Review and approve maintenance billing invoices and projects as per contracted agreements. Ensure consistent delivery of core operational and financial outputs on the account.
- Respond to inquiries on financial reports for Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, and open purchase orders.
- Deliver monthly reporting support on Contract and Business Unit Reviews.
- Assist in ensuring compliance with Health & Safety requirements, including HSE reporting and promoting a safe work environment. Maintain QHSE documentation and ensure it is available using company systems.
- Gather and analyse data to identify and solve complex problems that arise with little or no precedent. May recommend new techniques.
- Impact own team and other teams whose work activities are closely related.
- Suggest improvements to existing processes and solutions to improve the efficiency of the team.

Experience Required:
- A comprehensive understanding of a range of processes, procedures, systems, and concepts within own job function.
- Ability to evaluate and communicate unusual and/or complex content in a concise and logical way.
- In-depth knowledge of Microsoft Office products, including Word, Excel, and Outlook.
- Strong organisational skills with an advanced inquisitive mindset.
- Advanced mathematical skills with the ability to calculate percentages, discounts, and mark-ups.

DISCLAIMER

This job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this role. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, and qualifications required of employees assigned to the job. CBRE reserves the right to modify this job description at any time without notice.

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant

Location: Newport

Salary: £27,810 per annum

Hours: 40 hours per week

Job Type: Full-Time, Permanent

Working Arrangement: Fully office-based

The Opportunity

Môrwell Talent Solutions is working with an established organisation to recruit an organised, efficient and proactive Accounts Assistant to join their finance team.

This is a varied, hands-on role combining day-to-day accounts responsibilities with general administrative duties. We are looking for someone who takes pride in keeping things organised, works methodically and accurately, and is confident taking ownership of their workload.

The successful candidate will enjoy variety, be comfortable managing competing priorities and be happy getting involved wherever needed to support the smooth running of the department. Strong communication skills are essential, particularly the confidence to pick up the phone, speak with colleagues, suppliers and customers, and proactively follow up on outstanding queries.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with previous accounts experience who enjoys working in a busy team and is looking for a varied role where they can contribute to the wider business.

Key Responsibilities

Accounts & Finance
- Process supplier invoices and assist with purchase ledger administration, payments and supplier account reconciliations.
- Support sales ledger activities, including raising invoices, monitoring outstanding balances and chasing overdue payments.
- Complete bank reconciliations and reconcile payments received through various channels.
- Assist with daily income reconciliations, ensuring financial records are accurate and up to date.
- Investigate discrepancies, resolve queries and liaise with relevant departments, suppliers and customers.
- Support month-end activities, financial reporting and other accounts duties as required.

Administration & Communication
- Provide general administrative support to the finance department and wider business.
- Maintain accurate records, spreadsheets, filing systems and financial documentation.
- Respond to telephone calls and emails from colleagues, suppliers and customers in a professional and timely manner.
- Confidently pick up the phone to chase information, resolve queries and follow up on outstanding issues.
- Liaise with other departments to ensure information is communicated effectively and tasks are completed promptly.
- Manage competing priorities, use initiative and ensure actions are followed through to completion.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for someone who is highly organised, methodical and proactive, with a keen eye for detail and the ability to manage their workload efficiently.

You will be a confident communicator who is comfortable speaking to people at all levels, happy to undertake both accounts and administrative duties, and willing to take ownership rather than waiting to be told what needs doing.

Essential skills and experience:
- Previous experience in an accounts or finance environment.
- An understanding of purchase ledger and sales ledger processes.
- Good IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel.
- Strong organisational, numerical and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including confidence using the telephone.
- A professional approach to accuracy, confidentiality and teamwork.
- The ability to work independently, prioritise tasks and use initiative.

Experience within a hotel, hospitality or similar multi-department environment would be advantageous, as would familiarity with accounting software or property management systems.

What's on Offer?
- Salary of £27,810 per annum.
- 20 days' annual leave plus bank holidays.
- Statutory pension scheme.
- Life assurance scheme.
- The opportunity to join an established finance team in a varied role combining accounts, administration and communication.

Interested?

If you are an organised, efficient and proactive individual who enjoys a varied role, takes pride in getting things done and is confident picking up the phone, we would love to hear from you.

Please contact Môrwell Talent Solutions for further information or to discuss the opportunity in confidence.

title: School Administrator
description:
Job Title: School Administrator
Responsible to: Headteacher / School Business Manager
Salary Grade: 92 - 100 a day
Hours: School ter times
Contract: Temporary

1. Job Purpose

To provide an efficient, professional and effective administrative service, supporting the day-to-day operation of the school. The postholder will support the Headteacher, staff, pupils, parents/carers and governors, contributing to the school's vision, values and commitment to improving learner outcomes, wellbeing and inclusion.

The role will support Welsh Government education priorities, including the Curriculum for Wales, safeguarding, Additional Learning Needs (ALN), equality and inclusion, and the promotion of Welsh language and culture.

2. Key Duties and Responsibilities

The School Administrator will:
- Provide a welcoming, professional first point of contact for parents/carers, pupils, visitors, staff and external agencies.
- Manage telephone calls, emails, correspondence and general enquiries, ensuring information is communicated accurately and promptly.
- Provide administrative support to the Headteacher, senior leadership team, teaching staff and governors.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date pupil records, staff information and school management information systems.
- Support pupil admissions, transfers, leavers and transition arrangements.
- Record and monitor pupil attendance, follow up unexplained absences and produce attendance reports.
- Prepare letters, newsletters, reports, presentations, meeting papers and other school documentation.
- Organise meetings, appointments, school events, trips and visits.
- Support financial administration, including processing orders, invoices, payments and purchase requisitions in accordance with school procedures.
- Maintain effective filing, record-keeping and document management systems, ensuring information is stored securely.

3. Person Specification

Essential:
- Good standard of general education, including English and Mathematics, or equivalent experience.
- Experience in an administrative or customer-facing role.
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office.
- Excellent organisational, communication and time-management skills.
- Ability to maintain accurate records and handle confidential information.
- Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Desirable:
- Previous experience working within a school or educational setting.
- Knowledge of school management information systems.
- Experience of attendance and financial administration.

4. Welsh Government Framework and Professional Expectations

The postholder is expected to demonstrate professional behaviours that support the school's wider educational priorities, particularly:
- Collaboration: Working effectively with colleagues, families and external partners.
- Professional Learning: Engaging in training, reflection and continuous development.
- Innovation: Identifying opportunities to improve administrative systems and processes.
- Leadership: Demonstrating initiative, accountability and professionalism within the role.
- Pedagogy and learner-centred practice: Supporting an effective school environment in which all learners can thrive.

5. Safeguarding

The school is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. All staff are expected to share this commitment and undertake appropriate safeguarding training. Appointment will be subject to satisfactory pre-employment checks, including an appropriate DBS check.

- Excellent communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively
- A proactive attitude and willingness to learn

What's on Offer?
- Salary of £28,000 per annum
- Opportunity to join a well-established financial services business

- Exposure to a broad range of finance responsibilities

title: Quality Administrator
description:
Administrators - Why You Should Apply

A new career, no degree needed: You don't need a lab or science background to become a QC Administrator here. Everything is fully trained, so if you've got sharp admin skills and an eye for detail, this is your way into the science sector without going back to university.

Build your day around you: Flexitime lets you start any time between 7:30am and 9:30am and finish between 3:30pm and 5:30pm. Do the school run, beat the traffic, or get to the gym while it's quiet, then shape your hours around your life.

Grow with a busy lab: New business is coming in fast, and the small team is set to expand, so you're joining at the point where there's real room to move up.

Your salary, benefits & hours of work
- 27,000 and annual bonus
- Flexitime: start any time between 7:30am and 9:30am, finish between 3:30pm and 5:30pm
- Monday to Friday, no weekends
- Full training from day one
- No weekend or bank holiday working, with a shutdown from Christmas to the New Year.
- Holidays 24 days plus 8 Bank Holidays (increasing with length of service - one extra day for every 5 years to a maximum of 25 years)

What you'll do as the Quality Control Administrator

You'll keep the Quality Control project team running smoothly, handling the admin that gets samples tested and results back to customers.
- Book stability and project samples into the QC systems
- Organise despatch of samples to partner testing laboratories, raising purchase orders and labelling correctly
- Collect and trend data, create Certificates of Analysis and draft customer quotes
- Complete and archive records, keeping the lab audit-ready
- Prepare reagents and run basic sample checks once trained
- Order consumables and support improvements across the lab

What you'll need to apply for the Quality Administrator
- Strong, hands-on administration experience with a genuine eye for detail
- Good computer literacy (Microsoft Office 365) and happy to learn new systems.

title: Estates Coordinator
description:
Safran is an international high-technology group operating in the fields of aerospace (propulsion, equipment and interiors), space and defense. Its mission is to contribute sustainably to a safer world, where air transport becomes ever more environmentally friendly, comfortable and accessible. Present on every continent, Safran was ranked second in the Aerospace & Defense sector in TIME magazine's World's Best Companies 2025 ranking.
With more than one million seats installed across the fleets of the world's leading airlines, Safran Seats is one of the global leaders in passenger, crew, aircraft and helicopter seating, delivering innovative, high value-added solutions.

Based at Imperial Park, you will work with the Estates and Services team to ensure the seamless provision of facility management services to the building.
Working with Hard and Soft Services teams, you will ensure that all activity is undertaken in line with best practice, with engagement of relevant stakeholders and in accordance with Health and Safety guidance.
- As a highly organised individual, you will help drive efficiency and support wider strategic Estates and Services topics including Risk Management, Security Management and Continuous Improvement initiatives
- Drive a safety first culture with all suppliers and contractors ensuring all work is backed up with adequate Risk and Method Statements (RAMS) before commencing any works.
- First point of contact for day to day security issues and escalation at site level.
- First point of contact for cleaning and waste issues and escalations at site level.
- First point of contact for site based projects ensuring stakeholders are kept informed of any potential disruption.
- Conduct the daily SQCDP process and represent Estates and Services at any stakeholder operational meeting.
- Develop the space management database ensuring information remains up to date and reflective of current organisation footprint
- Manage stakeholder requirements for office accommodation and specification development for new projects.
- Ensure building drawings are up to date and reflect current office and industrial layout.
Manage the Estates and Services Risk Register and all associated risk assessments.
- Interface on all Insurance Management matters ensuring building changes and developments are recorded.
- Maintain the Site Services Business Continuity plan ensuring it is communicated and updated.
- Be the first point of contact on Facilities and Property matters for Safran Real Estate, building landlords and their agents for Imperial Park.
- Support on Safran global standards and process for Estates and Services activities where required.
- Deputise for Technical Services and Soft Services Leads for operational activities at Imperial Park.

Technical / Job Specific Competencies
- Supplier Management
- Facility Management
- Waste Management
- Budget Management and Control
- Relevant H&S Qualification (IOSH, NEBOSH etc.)
- Excellent IT literacy skills in MS Outlook, Word, Excel and PowerPoint
Behavioural Competencies
- Exemplary Organisation Skills to drive high performance attitude and behaviours into the supply chain
- Excellent Leadership skills to drive continuous improvement and innovation
- A 'Can do' attitude with a willingness to develop and foster new skills to achieve
challenging objectives
- Clear and concise communication with an understanding of the need to keep stakeholders engaged for the duration of a project
